EXPORTS REACHABILITY PROBED AT RUNTIME (method designed by pij-related-koala, run by the o-prime in this repo; script committed as scripts/exports-reachability-probe.mjs). An exports map does not merely FAIL TO LIST a subpath, it FORBIDS it — reachability is a runtime fact (ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED), not a barrel-file reading, so the module exports it and a consumer can import it are different questions. Probe run against a scratch project with node_modules/@ai-substrate/dd symlinked to this repo, on node v24.7.0, WITH POSITIVE CONTROLS (a zero result proves nothing if the probe is broken): control 1 root export reachable PASS, control 2 undeclared path forbidden PASS, control 3 declared-path-wrong-extension forbidden PASS. RESULT: 11 of 12 consumed subpaths reachable; ./plan is FORBIDDEN with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. This confirms koala paper check as a runtime fact and sharpens OQ-2 materially: the question is not merely whether plan SHOULD be public but that under todays map harness CANNOT CONSUME IT AT ALL — a hard error at import, not a workaround, affecting 9 symbols across acts/plan/index.ts and acts/plan/pr-body.ts. SECOND FINDING, a real defect the probe surfaced incidentally: the root export . resolves to dist/index.js which IS THE BIN ENTRY (src/index.ts carries the node shebang and calls main()), so import @ai-substrate/dd EXECUTES THE CLI as an import side effect, printing help to stdout, and yields ZERO named exports. koala predicted this from the same defect in harness-engineering own package. Not blocking harness (it imports subpaths, never the root) but freezing the map would freeze the defect. NOT yet wired into just checks — deliberate hold, since a new gate needs its ci.yml twin and a CI run was in flight.

CORRECTION to the drift-window claim recorded at 53d07df (append-only; the o-prime relayed the superseded version to Jordan and has corrected him directly). WHAT SURVIVES: forward-port debt on the consumed surface is STILL ZERO — nothing is on upstream main, and the d08f4942-to-origin/main diff across the three files is still empty. That measurement stands. WHAT WAS WRONG: I recorded that the branch was empty so the ownership call could be made BEFORE THE FIRST BYTE IS WRITTEN. The bytes are written — 199 insertions / 26 deletions across 7 files, UNCOMMITTED in a separate upstream worktree, which no branch probe run from another checkout can see. SECOND CORRECTION: the live consumed surface is TWO files, not three — core/validate.ts is genuinely untouched (its defect was ruled into a later PR), so four symbols are in play (PlanDocument, itemKey, buildPlanIndex, resolveMapSeed), not seven. THE ACCURATE WINDOW, stated once: the changes EXIST, are UNCOMMITTED, are UNDER REVIEW, and nothing is on main — debt is zero and the change set is still fully reversible, but it is ONE COMMIT from existing. Hours, not before-anyone-starts. THE LESSON (koala, about its own method): it probed the BRANCH and concluded about the WORK, and an empty branch is not an absence of work. Uncommitted worktree state is invisible to git log, to a diff against a merge-base, AND to gh pr list — so ALL THREE INSTRUMENTS IT REACHED FOR SHARE ONE BLIND SPOT, and their agreement proved nothing. AGREEMENT BETWEEN INSTRUMENTS THAT SHARE A BLIND SPOT IS NOT CORROBORATION. My own re-derivation at 53d07df used two of those same three instruments, so it confirmed the true part (debt zero) and inherited the same blindness on the false part.
